articles.title: OCVibe’s Scott Frick On Building a $5B District Around Anaheim’s Honda Center
articles.narrative: OCVibe, a 100-acre master-planned district surrounding Anaheim's Honda Center, is being privately financed by Henry and Susan Samueli, owners of the Anaheim Ducks, with a $5 billion investment. The development will transform surface parking lots into a dense mixed-use environment featuring 170,000 square feet of office space, over 2,000 apartments, two hotels, and more than 35 dining concepts, alongside 20 acres of parks. The project aims to create a year-round destination, addressing a gap in Orange County for cultural centers and high-quality urban living, while also enhancing the pre- and post-event experience for arena visitors. The first major public-facing components, including a market hall, a 5,000-capacity concert venue, and a mass-timber office building, are slated for completion in 2027, with overall project delivery expected through 2030-2031.

data_points.notable_features: Includes 20 acres of parks and plazas, a 5,000-capacity concert venue, and a 50,000-square-foot market hall named Katella Commons. The Weave is a six-story mass-timber office building.
data_points.project_notes: The development is privately financed by the Samueli family. Construction began approximately three years ago. The first phase involved building parking structures to free up surface lots, with parking decks delivered in 2025 and 2026. The Honda Center will host indoor volleyball during the 2028 Olympics.

articles.market_intelligence: Orange County is described as very suburban with high rents and supply constraints, with inventory growth slowing to less than 1% annually. Anaheim attracts 30 million visitors a year due to attractions like Disneyland and the convention center. Office construction is currently dry, with a 'flight to quality' trend towards Class A-plus office spaces.

articles.title: Pinnacle Group Sells Rights to Upper West Side Apartment Tower for $88M
articles.narrative: Pinnacle Group has sold its lease rights and a 50% stake in the land rights for a 173-unit apartment building at 323 West 96th Street in Manhattan to Lightstone Group for approximately $88 million. The transaction, which included an $11 million surplus for bondholders, follows Pinnacle's recent offloading of a $128 million condominium and commercial portfolio across New York City. The sale is part of Pinnacle's efforts to address significant debt after placing a large rent-stabilized portfolio into bankruptcy last year.

data_points.address: 323 West 96th Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: 15-story apartment building located at the corner of East 96th Street and First Avenue.
data_points.project_notes: Pinnacle Group secured the leasehold in 2007 and acquired a land rights stake in 2016 for $27 million. The property carried an existing loan balance of approximately $65 million as of March 2026, which was transferred to a Barclays-sponsored CMBS trust in 2023.

articles.title: At New York City Council Hearing on Pied-à-Terre Tax, Complaints of a Sloppy Rollout
articles.narrative: The New York City Council held a hearing to evaluate the problematic rollout of the city's new pied-à-terre tax, which has been criticized for its sloppy implementation and the publication of a broad list of potential second homes. Councilmember Gale Brewer highlighted that the Department of Finance's list included up to 900,000 properties, far exceeding estimates of actual second homes, and placed an undue burden on homeowners to prove primary residency. The Real Estate Board of New York also expressed concerns about the tax's administration, urging the city to pause implementation until it can ensure fairness and accuracy. Despite a temporary restraining order, an appeals court has allowed the city to continue implementing the tax while litigation is pending.

data_points.project_notes: The pied-à-terre tax targets single- to three-family second homes valued over $5 million, or co-ops and condos over $1 million, with potential implementation by January 2027.

articles.title: Betting on South Beach Luxury Shopping, Vivienne Westwood Plans to Open Store
articles.narrative: Luxury fashion brand Vivienne Westwood is moving forward with plans to open a boutique in Miami Beach's South Beach, nearly two years after acquiring the property at 736 Collins Avenue. The brand submitted an application to build out the 1921-era building, which will feature a ground-floor retail space, executive offices on the second floor, and a bridal showroom with a rooftop deck on the top floor. The project aims to blend the building's Art Deco and Mediterranean Revival heritage with contemporary design elements, signaling a bet on the resurgence of high-end retail in the South Beach area.

data_points.notable_features: The project honors the building's 1921 Art Deco and Mediterranean Revival heritage while introducing contemporary elements like Florida limestone cladding, polished brass storefront, and a landmark pink neon signature.
data_points.project_notes: The 14,692-square-foot building was previously acquired by Vivienne Westwood in 2024 for $6 million.

articles.title: Get to Know the Broker: Vickey Barron of Compass
articles.narrative: This article profiles Vickey Barron, an associate broker at Compass, highlighting her career achievements and philosophy. Barron emphasizes that her purpose in real estate is to serve people and help them find homes, rather than focusing solely on commissions or sales volume. She recounts her most significant deal as helping a 93-year-old woman negotiate a life estate to remain in her West Village townhouse after its sale, underscoring the human impact of her work.

articles.title: JPI to Develop $90M Multifamily Project in Northwest Austin
articles.narrative: JPI is set to develop Jefferson Pearson Ranch, a $90 million multifamily project in northwest Austin. The development will feature 342 units across four buildings, offering a mix of studios to three-bedroom residences. Construction is expected to commence shortly, with an anticipated completion in 2028.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities will include a pool, fitness center, resident lounge, outdoor grilling and dining stations, a dog park and coworking space. Located within the 156-acre Pearson Ranch master-planned development.

articles.title: Apricus, ABR Capital Buy 18.5-Acre Industrial Outdoor Storage Facility in Northwest Houston
articles.narrative: A joint venture between Apricus Realty Capital and ABR Capital Partners has acquired an 18.5-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facility in northwest Houston. The property, which includes 53,000 square feet of warehouse and service facilities, was fully leased at the time of sale. JLL arranged the acquisition financing for the transaction.

data_points.address: 11403 N. Houston Rosslyn Road, Houston, TX

articles.title: Alcon Research Signs Industrial Lease Renewal, Expansion in Fort Worth
articles.narrative: Alcon Research LLC, a company focused on eye care innovation, has renewed and expanded its industrial lease in Fort Worth, Texas. The company's footprint now totals approximately 385,000 square feet. The landlord, TA Realty, was represented by Holt Lunsford Commercial, while Colliers represented the tenant.

articles.title: PENN Entertainment to Invest $195M to Relocate Riverboat Casino in New Orleans
articles.narrative: PENN Entertainment plans to invest $195 million to relocate its Boomtown Casino & Hotel New Orleans riverboat casino to an adjacent landside property, pending regulatory approval. The new development will span 140,000 square feet and feature a rebranded Hollywood Casino New Orleans, expected to open in 2029. This project marks PENN's fourth landside relocation of a riverboat casino, which the company intends to finance with cash on hand.

data_points.notable_features: Will include approximately 875 slot machines, 45 table games, a retail sportsbook, and multiple dining options.
data_points.project_notes: The existing riverboat casino will be vacated upon the new property's opening, but the existing hotel is expected to remain open. This is the fourth landside relocation of a riverboat casino for the developer.

articles.title: Chicago’s The Goldie Initiative announces 34 new Goldie Scholars for 2026-2027 academic year
articles.narrative: The Goldie Initiative, a non-profit organization, has announced 34 new Goldie Scholars for the 2026-2027 academic year, bringing the total cohort to 45 women pursuing graduate degrees in commercial real estate. This year saw a record 145 applications, a 51% increase from the previous year, making it the most competitive selection cycle in the program's history. The expansion of the cohort was made possible by the support of charitable foundations and individual donors, including new partnerships with the Sue Ling Gin Foundation Trust and continued collaboration with the Debbie Frank Legacy Fund, CREW Chicago, and the Annexstad Family Foundation. The incoming scholars represent 23 universities nationwide, with several institutions participating for the first time, reflecting the initiative's growing reach and impact in identifying future female leaders in the industry.

articles.title: SVN|Chicago Commercial closes sale of 6,000-square-foot retail property in Chicago’s North Center neighborhood
articles.narrative: SVN | Chicago Commercial recently facilitated the sale of a 6,000-square-foot retail property in Chicago's North Center neighborhood for $1,507,500. The two-story asset garnered significant interest, receiving multiple offers and ultimately selling for 8% above its asking price, with the transaction closing in under a month.

data_points.project_notes: Sold for 8% above asking price, moving from listing to closing in less than one month.

articles.title: Northmarq closes refinance for 342-unit multifamily community in Houston
articles.narrative: Northmarq's Houston Debt + Equity team has successfully secured refinancing for The Mill Residences, a 342-unit mid-rise multifamily community in Houston's East End. The loan was arranged on behalf of Triten Real Estate Partners through one of Northmarq's correspondent balance sheet lending relationships. The property, built in 2025, offers luxury Class A apartments and resort-style amenities, benefiting from its prime location with access to public transit, dining, entertainment, and the burgeoning arts district.

data_points.notable_features: Luxury Class A studio, one-, and two-bedroom apartments with stone countertops, high ceilings, and multiple interior finish packages. Amenities include a fitness center, yoga studio, poolside cabanas, and a quiet lounge with high-speed connectivity for remote workers. Located in Houston's East End with convenient access to public transit, dining, live entertainment, and the arts district.

articles.title: Provider of critical infrastructure services signs 25,352-square-foot lease in Fort Bend County mixed-use development
articles.narrative: Primoris Services Corporation, a Fortune 500 infrastructure services provider, has signed a 25,352-square-foot office lease at 2150 Town Square Place within the Sugar Land Town Square mixed-use development in Fort Bend County, Texas. This lease comes as the development undergoes a significant redevelopment initiative, including a refreshed lobby and new amenity suite, aimed at enhancing the tenant experience and attracting corporate employers. Primoris is expected to begin occupancy in 2027.

data_points.address: 2150 Town Square Place, Sugar Land, TX
data_points.notable_features: Mixed-use development undergoing a $12.5 million reinvestment to enhance tenant experience, including a refreshed lobby, new amenity suite with an F&B-powered tenant lounge, conference center, fitness center, and café.
data_points.project_notes: The City of Sugar Land approved a $12.5 million reinvestment in 2025 for property enhancements at Town Square One (2150 Town Square Place) and Town Square Two (2277 Plaza Drive). Renovations began in mid-2026 and are expected to be complete by spring 2027.

articles.title: Block & Company brokers sale of 12,297-square-foot office building in Mission
articles.narrative: Balls Food Stores has acquired a 12,927-square-foot office building at 5830 Woodson in Mission, Kansas, to serve as its new corporate headquarters. The move supports the company's expanding network of grocery stores across the Kansas City metropolitan area. Block & Company, Inc., Realtors, represented the buyer in this transaction.

data_points.notable_features: Centrally located in Mission, a well-connected community in Johnson County.

articles.title: AmTrustRE Brings Financial District Office Tower to 100% Occupancy
articles.narrative: AmTrustRE has achieved 100% occupancy at its 59 Maiden Lane office tower in Manhattan's Financial District, a significant milestone ahead of the property's repositioning completion. The full occupancy was secured through a new 14,807-square-foot lease with ANV Group Holdings Ltd. and a 58,164-square-foot renewal by London Fischer LLP. This achievement validates AmTrustRE's investment strategy of repositioning well-located assets and enhancing the tenant experience.

data_points.address: 59 Maiden Ln., New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: The property is undergoing facade and lobby renovations, expected in 2027, and a redesigned public plaza, slated for completion later in 2026.

articles.title: CBRE Arranges 118K-SF Price Zone Lease in Commerce
articles.narrative: CBRE has arranged a nearly 118,000-square-foot industrial lease at Harris Business Center in Commerce, CA, for Price Zone, a wholesale distributor and importer of consumer goods. This transaction enables Price Zone to consolidate its operations from three separate facilities into a single, more efficient location. The deal was mutually beneficial, providing the tenant with desired operational efficiency and economics, while helping the landlord maximize occupancy within the business park.

data_points.notable_features: The facility features a 24-foot warehouse clearance, 19 dock-high loading positions, three ground-level doors, and rail service provided by the Los Angeles Junction Railway.

articles.title: Terreno Adds to NYC Portfolio with Red Hook Acquisition
articles.narrative: Terreno Realty Corporation, an industrial real estate owner and operator, has acquired an industrial property in Red Hook, Brooklyn, for approximately $26.3 million. The property, which includes a 28,000-square-foot distribution building on 1.5 acres, is fully leased to a maritime goods and services provider. This acquisition further expands Terreno's significant industrial portfolio in the New York City/Northern New Jersey market.

data_points.address: 659 Court St., New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: The property provides two grade-level loading positions, parking for 70 cars, and riparian access.
data_points.project_notes: The estimated stabilized cap rate for the acquisition is 5.2%.

articles.title: Building Block Foundation Fund: CRE Industry’s Way to Make a Difference
articles.narrative: The Building Block Foundation Fund, a non-profit organization run by commercial real estate professionals, focuses its fundraising efforts on networking events for the CRE industry. The fund aims to make a meaningful impact on Orange County charities that support at-risk youth in areas like education, housing, mentorship, and protection from exploitation. The organization has raised over $3 million and supports charities such as Project Access, Hope Ignites Southern California, Everfree, Joyful Child Foundation, Kidworks, Orangewood Children’s Foundation, HomeAid, and Hope Builders. Its annual 'Endless Summer' event brings together hundreds of CRE peers for an industry celebration and networking opportunity.

articles.title: Prism Partners Trades Two-Building Edison Lofts for $131M
articles.narrative: Prism Partners and its capital partners have sold Edison Lofts, a 334-unit luxury multifamily community in West Orange, NJ, to Sym Investments for $131 million. The property, which includes nearly 19,000 square feet of retail space, attracted significant investor interest due to its blend of historic conversion and modern amenities, strong occupancy, and favorable tax pilot program. Cushman & Wakefield also arranged a $91.7 million acquisition loan from New York Life for the buyer.

data_points.notable_features: The community includes a 300-unit conversion of the historic Thomas Edison Battery Building and a 34-unit ground-up residential building.
data_points.project_notes: The acquisition loan features a full-term interest-only structure.

articles.title: These 15 Lenders Are Leading The $1.3T Data Center Debt Surge

This surge in financing is driven by the explosive growth in data center construction across the country, with an accounting of 4,296 facilities revealing the key financial institutions supporting this sector.
articles.market_intelligence: The data center debt market has reached $1.3 trillion, indicating significant investment and growth in the sector. There are 4,296 data center facilities accounted for across the country.

articles.title: AvalonBay, Equity Residential Selling Boston Towers As Part Of Merger Settlement
articles.narrative: Vivmark, a newly formed entity resulting from the merger of AvalonBay and Equity Residential, has agreed to sell two multifamily properties in Boston. This divestiture is part of a settlement reached with the state, indicating a regulatory requirement for the merger's approval.

articles.title: Suburban Industrial Campus Trades For $47M: The Boston Deal Sheet
articles.narrative: This article is a deal sheet covering multiple transactions in the Boston market, including the sale of a suburban industrial campus for $47 million. Other notable activities include an office lease signed by the Boston Red Sox near Fenway Park and a construction loan secured for a downtown conversion project.

articles.title: Oak Brook Investor Scoops Up Suburban Multifamily Community: The Chicago Deal Sheet
articles.narrative: JVM Realty has acquired a 280-unit multifamily community in Oswego, Illinois, expanding its portfolio of suburban Chicago investments. This transaction underscores the continued investor interest in well-located residential assets within the broader Chicago metropolitan area.

articles.title: Shapiro Turns On Pennsylvania Data Centers With Restrictive Executive Order
articles.narrative: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro has issued an executive order imposing new restrictions on data center developments across the state. This move comes in response to growing public opposition and concerns regarding the impact of these facilities. The order is expected to introduce stricter guidelines for future data center projects, potentially affecting their planning and operational aspects.
